Conversely, major downside risks include a sudden and severe economic recession, aggressive monetary tightening by central banks beyond current expectations, the escalation of geopolitical conflicts, or unforeseen market shocks. Events such as a new global health crisis, major natural disasters, or significant regulatory changes in key industries could also trigger outcomes well below the lower bounds of the forecasted ranges.
